presentation.label: MIDI
presentation.summary: A machine that sequences an external synth from a Rytm track: notes, chords, pitch bend, mod wheel, pressure and six CC lanes, all lockable.
presentation.overview: Pick MIDI, the last entry of the machine list, as a track's machine and that track plays an external synth over MIDI instead of a sound. Its trigs send their note, velocity and length, with two chord notes; pitch bend, mod wheel, channel pressure and six CC lanes follow p-locks, lock-only steps and the LFO.
highlights: Every value is a sound parameter: p-locks, the LFO, conditions, swing and kits work as for any machine.
Lock trigs send controller changes without a note.
A lane that is OFF sends nothing, which is not the same as sending 0.
Chords: two extra notes per trig, as semitone offsets.
usage: Connect the Rytm's MIDI OUT to a synth listening on channel 1. Select a track, open its machine list on the SYNTH page and choose MIDI.
Place trigs and play: the synth plays the trigs' notes. Set N2 to +7 for a fifth on every trig.
On the AMP page turn HLD (C1#) to 74, then on the SYNTH page turn CC1: the synth's CC 74 follows. Lock CC1 on a trig, or place a lock trig (FUNC + TRIG) with a CC1 lock to change it without a note.

access.location: The machine list of any track, then its SYNTH, FILTER and AMP pages.
steps: Select a track and open its machine list on the SYNTH page; choose MIDI.
SYNTH page: N2, N3, PB, MW, AT and the CC1-CC3 values.
FILTER page: ATK, DEC and SUS are the CC4-CC6 values.
AMP page: ATK is the channel, HLD to PAN the six lanes' CC numbers (turn right from OFF to switch a lane on), VOL which of PB, MW and AT send.

controls.name: N2
controls.doc: SYNTH A. A second note, OFF or -24 to +24 semitones from the trig's note.

controls.name: N3
controls.doc: SYNTH B. A third note, OFF or -24 to +24 semitones from the trig's note.

controls.name: PB
controls.doc: SYNTH C. Pitch bend, -63 to +63, sent 14-bit and centred when SND includes P.

controls.name: MW
controls.doc: SYNTH D. Mod wheel (CC 1), 0 to 127, when SND includes M.

controls.name: AT
controls.doc: SYNTH E. Channel pressure, 0 to 127, when SND includes A.

controls.name: CC1-CC6
controls.doc: SYNTH F-H and FILTER ATK, DEC, SUS. Each lane's value, 0 to 127, sent on its CC number while the lane is on.

controls.name: CHN
controls.doc: AMP ATK. The MIDI channel, 1 to 16.

controls.name: C1#-C6#
controls.doc: AMP HLD, DEC, OVR, DEL, REV, PAN. Each lane's CC number, OFF or 1 to 119. Turn right from OFF to switch the lane on, below 1 to switch it off.

controls.name: SND
controls.doc: AMP VOL. Which of pitch bend, mod wheel and pressure send.

limitations: Tested on one unit; several MIDI tracks at once, scenes and pattern changes are not tested yet.
Pads, chromatic play and MIDI in do not play tracks on the MIDI machine yet; the sequencer does.
Retrigs send their first note only; no program change or slides yet.
The AMP and FILTER knobs keep their stock labels; the value text says what each is.

claims: ui:SYNTH page of the MIDI machine
ui:FILTER ATK DEC SUS value texts on tracks on the MIDI machine
ui:AMP page values and turns on tracks on the MIDI machine

load.conditions: Measure with every track playing, parameters modulated and the mod at its heaviest setting.

hardware.summary: Test builds ME09 to ME17 on the author's unit over DIN (and USB once), a synth's MIDI read on a computer monitor: silent track, notes and chords, LEN and INF, STOP, lane values and locks, lock trigs, live PB/MW/AT and CC knobs, SND OFF, LFO on a lane, swing and microtiming, mute, save and power cycle, leaving the machine. ME17 last: leave and return, then PLAY, with no stray CC.
limitations: One unit, one MIDI track at a time; scenes, performances, conditions and pattern changes not tested.
No CPU load measured on the unit.

tests.summary: Developer's unit, OS 1.74, ME09-ME17 over DIN and USB: silent track, chords, LEN, lanes, live PB/MW/AT, p-locks, lock trigs, LFO on a lane, swing and microtiming, mute, save and power cycle, leaving the machine. Earlier builds in rytm-emu. See TESTING.md.
